description:
I’m an Industrial & Production Engineering student at SUST, passionate about AI/ML, IoT, robotics, and biomedical innovation. Our project, MISSION-HEALTH DIGITAL TWIN, aims to predict astronaut health risks by analyzing physiological data, sleep, mission workload, and spacecraft environments.

We’re seeking teammates skilled in AI/ML, software development, biomedical science, data analysis, and electronics. Curiosity, teamwork, and creativity matter most!
summary:
ASTRAVIVE is a browser-based health simulator built to track and reduce astronaut health risks on long-duration space missions. Deep-space communication delays make real-time telemedicine impossible. To bridge that gap, the platform Astravive pairs NASA Human Research Program physiological models with explainable machine learning and Monte Carlo forecasting to predict how a crew member's health will change over time.

It focuses on five interconnected risks:
- Bone mineral density loss
- Cardiovascular plasma volume contraction
- Spaceflight-Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS)
- Ionizing radiation exposure
- Circadian sleep fragmentation

Using data from NASA's Open Science Data Repository (including the Inspiration4 studies OSD-575 and OSD-569, as well as the OSD-51 bed rest analog), ASTRAVIVE gives flight surgeons a side-by-side simulator (Scenario A vs. Scenario B) to test different countermeasures and catch health issues before they cause permanent harm.
details:
Day 42 of a Mars mission. An astronaut wakes up with blurred vision, a headache, and slower reflexes than usual. On Earth, a flight surgeon would order tests that morning. Here, a radio message takes up to about 22 minutes to reach Earth, and the only medical care available is whatever is already in the habitat. Several of the risks below are much easier to manage if you see them coming.

ASTRAVIVE is an open-science digital twin of crew health for long-duration missions.

What It Does & How It Works

It tracks five risks that feed into each other in microgravity:

  1. Bone density loss: the skeleton gradually deconditions.
  2. Cardiovascular contraction: fluid shifts reduce plasma volume.
  3. Spaceflight-Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS): rising intracranial pressure that damages vision.
  4. Circadian sleep debt: fragmented sleep that builds into cognitive fatigue.
  5. Ionizing radiation: cumulative dose, tracked against NASA career limits.

We avoided a single black-box model. Long-term physical trends come from published NASA Human Research Program differential equations. Short-term wearable signals, like heart rate variability and electrodermal activity, go through small Scikit-learn models. The main feature is a Scenario A vs. Scenario B simulator. A flight surgeon changes exercise, sleep schedules, or CO₂ scrubbing and sees how the outcome shifts.

Tools, Software & Data Used

  • Languages and core tech: Python 3.10+, JavaScript (HTML5 Canvas), Streamlit
  • Machine learning and math: Scikit-learn (Random Forest, HistGradientBoosting, Isolation Forest), NumPy, SciPy, SHAP (TreeExplainer)
  • Frontend: a custom aerospace HUD with 9 ARIA tabs, WCAG 2.2 AA compliant, no external runtime dependencies
  • Data: NASA OSDR spaceflight clinical datasets (OSD-575, OSD-569), the 60-day bed rest analog (OSD-51), ISS environmental sensor logs, RadLab radiation dosimetry, and space weather from NASA’s DONKI API

What Makes It Creative

Many space hackathon projects are either static dashboards or deep-learning models trained on tiny astronaut cohorts, sometimes N=4, which overfit badly. We did three things differently:

  • Dual-scenario simulation. You can compare a failing baseline against an optimized countermeasure side by side over 90 days.
  • Explainable alerts. When an alert fires, the system shows why. For example, high cabin CO₂ combined with poor sleep is pushing intracranial pressure up. A flight surgeon can check that reasoning instead of taking it on faith.
  • In-browser verification. A live test runner lets judges check model cross-validation and equation accuracy without installing anything.

Factors Considered & Ethical Responsibility

Every metric carries a provenance tag: MEASURED, PUBLIC, SIMULATED, or MODEL PREDICTION. Simulated values are never passed off as real telemetry. ASTRAVIVE is meant to support a flight surgeon’s judgment, not replace it.
